articles.title: Nobel Peace Prize 2026 goes to Navi Pillay — "peace and international law" — International Relations
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** The Norwegian Nobel Committee honoured South African jurist Navanethem (Navi) Pillay, 85, of Indian Tamil origin, for promoting peace and international law and for helping ensure war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide are prosecuted. It reads as a statement on the rules-based order. Useful for Mains IR/ethics: accountability, universal jurisdiction, role of international courts.
**Memorise:** 125th Peace Prize; 12 million SEK; ceremony Oslo, 10 Dec. Career: first woman to start a law practice in Natal (1967); defended Mandela; first woman of colour on SA High Court; judge at ICTR (helped establish rape as an act of genocide/crime against humanity); judge at ICC; UN High Commissioner for Human Rights; chaired UN Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory; reported to currently sit on the ICJ.
**Notebook:** GS2 – IR (International institutions)
**Static anchor:** Laxmikanth/Shankar IAS – "International Organisations: UN & ICJ" and Mrunal IR pillar "International Law". *Nudge:* add a one-line comparison table ICJ vs ICC vs ICTR; cross-link to "India not a party to the Rome Statute".

articles.title: 57th GST Council (8 Oct): arrest powers to go, prosecution threshold up to ₹5 crore — Economy
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** Part of a decriminalisation / ease-of-compliance push. Recommended: scrapping GST officers' power of arrest (the Finance Minister said prosecution remains where criminality is established, via a prima facie case), raising the prosecution threshold ₹1 crore → ₹5 crore, cutting the general penalty ₹25,000 → ₹10,000. Reports also mention no demand notice for tax below ₹10,000, a 5% GST (no ITC) for delivery services via e-commerce, and an officers' committee on ITC under Sec 16(2)(c). These are *recommendations* — require legislative/rule changes; FM said process reforms apply from **1 April 2027**.
**Memorise:** 57th meeting, 8 Oct 2026; Art 279A; recommendations persuasive, not binding (Mohit Minerals, 2022); Secs 69 (arrest) and 132 (offences/punishment) of CGST Act.
**Notebook:** GS3 – Economy (Taxation) / GS2 Federalism
**Static anchor:** Laxmikanth – Ch. on GST Council (Art 279A) ; Mrunal Economy pillar "Indirect taxes". *Nudge:* add "decriminalisation of economic offences" as a Mains example next to Jan Vishwas.

articles.title: World Bank's World Development Report 2026: "The Promise of Artificial Intelligence" — Reports & Indices
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** Released in New Delhi on 8 Oct (presented by Chief Economist Michael Kremer; launched by IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw with the IndiaAI Mission). Core message: AI can widen access to expertise and lift productivity in medical screening, farming advice and education, but gains depend on electricity, connectivity, compute, data, skills and institutions — a "full-stack" approach. India's AI-driven monsoon forecasts to farmers were cited as a lesson (Ethiopia adopting it).
**Memorise:** WDR = annual flagship of the World Bank; IndiaAI Mission – 7 pillars (compute, foundation-model innovation centre, AIKosh datasets platform, application development, FutureSkills, startup financing, safe & trusted AI). Minister's claims (sugarcane yield +40% in Baramati, TB detection +35%) are not report findings.
**Notebook:** GS3 – Sci-Tech / GS2 Governance
**Static anchor:** Mrunal "Reports & Indices" sheet (add WDR 2026); Spectrum/IT chapter on AI. *Nudge:* link with digital public infrastructure and IndiaAI Mission notes.

articles.title: Pre-COP31 in Nadi, Fiji: India presses balance of adaptation, mitigation and means of implementation — Environment
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** Pre-COP31 (5–8 Oct) was co-hosted by Australia, Fiji and Tuvalu (leaders' event in Tuvalu) to centre Pacific priorities. COP31 will be at **Antalya, Türkiye, 9–20 Nov 2026**, with **Australia presiding over negotiations** — an unusual split-hosting arrangement. Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav called for equal attention to adaptation, mitigation and means of implementation, upheld CBDR-RC "in letter and spirit", and argued against one-size-fits-all action.
**Memorise:** COP31 dates/venue/presidency above; India's three asks: adaptation parity, finance/tech/capacity-building, CBDR-RC.
**Notebook:** GS3 – Environment (Climate diplomacy) / GS2 IR
**Static anchor:** Shankar IAS – "UNFCCC, Kyoto, Paris"; Mrunal Environment pillar "COP timeline". *Nudge:* add COP31 row to the COP table and link to Article 6 notes (see JCM, 6 Oct).

articles.title: Government moves to cap trade margins at 30% of MRP on 110 anti-cancer drugs — Society (Health)
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** Reportedly decided (not yet notified; expected to be implemented this month) after a Supreme Court hearing on 22 Sep where the bench noted a drug with MRP ₹27,000 supplied to retailers at ₹2,700. Covers non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs — branded or generic, domestic or imported, patented or not; a health-department committee is finalising the list. Aim: curb mis-selling and exorbitant margins; ties to Right to Health (Art 21) and affordability.
**Memorise:** 110 drugs (35 patented); 30% of MRP; "trade margin rationalisation"; NPPA under Dept of Pharmaceuticals; status – sources-based reports.
**Notebook:** GS2 – Social Justice (Health)
**Static anchor:** Laxmikanth – Art 21 / DPSP Art 47; Mrunal Society pillar "Health policy". *Nudge:* cross-link NPPA/DPCO 2013 with Jan Aushadhi and price-control notes.

articles.title: Ministry of Finance: 57th GST Council meeting (8 Oct, Bharat Mandapam) — arrest powers scrapped, prosecution threshold raised to ₹5 crore, faster refunds
articles.text:
**Notebook: GS3 Economy (Taxation, Federal Finance) / GS2 Governance**

The Council, chaired by the Union Finance Minister, focused on process reform and decriminalisation, not rate changes. It recommends removing arrest powers of GST officers (omitting Section 69 CGST Act). Several outlets note that prosecution is not abolished, only its threshold is raised.

- Prosecution threshold up from ₹1 crore to ₹5 crore (limited to fraudulent ITC).
- No show-cause notice for demands below ₹10,000; notices already issued for such demands to be withdrawn (per press reports).
- Refund acknowledgement cut from 15 to 10 days; about 90% of export and inverted-duty refund claims to be sanctioned provisionally by the system.
- Inverted-duty refunds extended to input services from 1 Nov 2026; capital goods credit refundable from 1 Apr 2027.
- E-way bill interception only on specific intelligence, by an officer not below Joint Commissioner.
- Optional quarterly payment scheme for B2C businesses up to ₹5 crore turnover (in principle); 2% TDS on B2B scrap supplies.
- No rate changes.

*Why it matters:* ease of doing business, decriminalisation of tax law, and the Council's role in cooperative federalism (Art. 279A). Note that these are Council recommendations and need legislative or notification follow-up.

articles.title: Ministry of Ports, Shipping & Waterways: Sagarmanthan 2026 — 3rd edition of "The Great Oceans Dialogue" (New Delhi, 7–8 Oct)
articles.text:
**Notebook: GS2 International Relations / GS3 Economy (Infrastructure, Blue Economy)**

Organised by MoPSW with the Observer Research Foundation. The PM's message called for a "free, open, secure and rules-based" maritime order. The first edition was in Nov 2024.

- Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047 presented as a partnership offer (government estimate: about ₹80 lakh crore investment; top-five shipbuilding goal).
- Agenda tracks: India–EU Green Shipping Corridor; review of the India–Korea shipbuilding and logistics framework; IMEC governance; OECD Blue Economy Scoreboards; African corridors such as Lobito.
- Context figures cited: coastline 11,098.81 km, 12 major ports, about 95% of trade by volume by sea.
- Critical point: India's share of global shipbuilding is below 1%.

articles.title: Ministry of Women & Child Development: Departmental Summit on Women and Child Development (8–9 Oct, Sushma Swaraj Bhawan) — second in the PM's series of departmental summits
articles.text:
**Notebook: GS2 Governance (Centre–State, Welfare) / GS1 Society**

Aimed at cooperative federalism, with the vision "Suposhit, Surakshit and Sashakt Bharat". Participants were Centre and state leaders and officials. The PM was scheduled to address the valedictory session on 9 Oct; its outcomes could not be verified.

- Four themes: reimagining Anganwadi Centres (nutrition and early education); child protection systems; women's safety frameworks; effectiveness of women's empowerment schemes.
- Discussion topics: take-home ration and hot cooked meals quality, Poshan Tracker data quality, ECCE, impact of social media on children.

## Also worth a line (not independently verified from PIB text)
- GST Council: single-source mention of 5% optional GST on EV passenger transport and 5% on e-commerce delivery services by unregistered persons.
- Pre-COP31 (Fiji) and MoSPI Environmental-Economic Accounts Strategy: covered in the 9 Oct briefing, no new development found.

articles.title: WWF Living Planet Report 2026: monitored wildlife populations down 73% since 1970 — Environment
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** The 2026 edition, "The Science of Hope", reports the Living Planet Index (compiled with the Zoological Society of London) at an average 73% fall in monitored populations over 1970–2022. This is a change in average population size, not 73% of animals lost. Reports of this kind are standard prelims fodder (publisher, index, what the number means) and give Mains data on the biodiversity crisis, Kunming–Montreal GBF targets and Red List trends.
**Memorize:** 73% average decline, 1970–2022 (about 2.5% a year) | 35,803 populations of 5,790 species | roughly half of the tracked populations are stable or growing | biennial WWF report with the LPI from ZSL.
**Notebook:** GS3 Environment (Biodiversity — reports/indices).
**Static anchor:** Shankar IAS *Biodiversity* chapter (IUCN Red List, threats) and the "Reports & Indices" tab. *Nudge:* add the LPR 2026 line with the "average, not absolute" caveat, and cross-link to the National Red List Roadmap in your Wildlife Week notes.

articles.title: MoSPI's Environmental-Economic Accounts Strategy 2026–2030 — Economy
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** MoSPI has released the 2026–30 strategy, which builds on the 2022–26 one (material flow, ocean, energy, biodiversity and urban ecosystem accounts). It follows the UN SEEA-Central Framework and ties into the National Accounts Framework 2025. The idea is that natural capital should be visible in national accounts alongside GDP. It supports SDG 12 and SDG 15. *Reported domain counts differ by source, so do not memorize a number.*
**Memorize:** MoSPI (NSO) | period 2026–30 | UN SEEA-CF | natural-capital accounting is a supplement to, not a replacement of, GDP.
**Notebook:** GS3 Economy (Inclusive growth / National income) and GS3 Environment.
**Static anchor:** Ramesh Singh *National Income* chapter (GDP, GNP, Green GDP). *Nudge:* add "SEEA / natural capital accounts" under the national income concepts and cross-link to the 2022–26 strategy.

articles.title: INS Surya: India's first indigenous Fleet Support Ship launched at HSL, Visakhapatnam — Internal Security
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** The Defence Minister launched FSS-1 INS Surya, designed and built by Hindustan Shipyard Limited (a Defence Ministry PSU). Fleet support ships carry out at-sea replenishment, extending naval endurance and reach in the Indian Ocean Region. It is an Atmanirbhar Bharat in defence example. Reports mention helicopter-deck and self-defence features. *Tonnage and order size are inconsistent across sources, so do not memorize them.*
**Memorize:** FSS = underway replenishment ship | HSL, Visakhapatnam | first indigenously designed and built FSS.
**Notebook:** GS3 Internal Security (Defence indigenisation).
**Static anchor:** Spectrum / defence notes on the Navy's blue-water capability. *Nudge:* add under "Navy platforms" and cross-link to the IOR strategy (SAGAR/MAHASAGAR) notes.

articles.title: Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 2026: optogenetics — Science & Technology
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel were honoured for optogenetics, in which genetically targeted cells are controlled with light through channels such as channelrhodopsin, first found in algae. It is a tool for mapping neural circuits and for brain-disorder research. Physics (IceCube) and Chemistry (chirality) were covered earlier this week, so this completes the science trio.
**Memorize:** Deisseroth, Hegemann, Nagel | light-gated ion channels (channelrhodopsin, from algae) | genetic targeting + light.
**Notebook:** GS3 Science & Technology (Biotechnology).
**Static anchor:** Biotechnology / genetic engineering chapter of your science notes. *Nudge:* add "Optogenetics" next to CRISPR and gene therapy, and note it as a research tool rather than a therapy.

articles.title: Ministry of Health & Family Welfare: JOSH Teams launched under TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan (8 Oct, Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi)
articles.text:
Union Health Minister J.P. Nadda launched youth-led "JOSH" teams (reported as *Joint Squad for Health*) to push TB prevention, early diagnosis, treatment completion and stigma reduction. Volunteers identify vulnerable people, encourage testing and support patients through treatment. The initiative was built with the Ministries of Youth Affairs & Sports and Defence.
- Phase 1: 55 districts in 11 States/UTs; remaining districts to follow (all 804 districts joined the launch virtually).
- 6,347 JOSH squads of 31,429 MY Bharat volunteers and 26,794 NCC cadets.
- Cited WHO-based figures: India's TB incidence down 21% (global 12%); treatment coverage 92% (global 78%). 67,933 Panchayats in 697 districts declared TB Mukt in 2026.
- **Notebook:** GS2 Governance (Health) / GS2 Social Sector.

### Scheme-in-focus: **JOSH Teams (under TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan)**
- **Ministry:** Health & Family Welfare, with Youth Affairs & Sports and Defence (NCC).
- **Objective:** Community, youth-led support to end TB.
- **Features:** (1) Squads of MY Bharat volunteers and NCC cadets; (2) screening and testing drives for vulnerable groups; (3) treatment-adherence and nutrition support; (4) stigma reduction and healthy-habit promotion.
- **Coverage:** 55 districts / 11 States-UTs in phase 1, scaling nationwide.
- **Significance:** Uses youth and community capital to close the last-mile gap toward the TB elimination goal.

articles.title: Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation: Strategy for Environmental-Economic Accounts 2026–2030 (7 Oct)
articles.text:
A non-statutory, "self-evolving" five-year roadmap issued by the NSO, successor to the 2022–26 strategy. Based on the UN SEEA Central Framework and the 2013 Green National Accounts report.
- Accounts: forests, minerals, soil, land, water, carbon stock, environment-related activities, biodiversity and environment statistics.
- EnviStats India shifts to biennial publication; 18 States/UTs have notified Inter-Departmental Groups (per a secondary summary); aligned with the Kunming–Montreal GBF.
- **Why it matters:** Natural capital accounting lets GDP reflect resource depletion, supporting "green GDP" style policy.
- **Notebook:** GS3 Economy + Environment.

articles.title: Ministry of Electronics & IT (IndiaAI Mission): World Bank's World Development Report 2026 — "The Promise of Artificial Intelligence" launched in India (8 Oct, New Delhi)
articles.text:
Launched by Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw with the World Bank Group.
- Advice to developing countries: adopt, adapt, then advance, instead of building frontier models from scratch.
- Benefits depend on foundations: electricity, connectivity, compute, data, skills, institutions.
- Only 1 of 25 low-income countries has a national AI strategy.
- Secondary-summary figures (not checked against the report): about 4% of Indian jobs at immediate automation risk; AI talent pool ~50,460.
- **Notebook:** GS3 Sci-Tech / Economy; GS2 International Organisations (Reports).

articles.title: Ministry of Environment, Forest & Climate Change: India at the informal pre-COP31 ministerial in Fiji (7 Oct) *(single secondary source)*
articles.text:
Co-hosted by Australia, Fiji and Tuvalu. India's line: judge COP31 (Antalya, Türkiye, November 2026) by implementation, not new targets; honour existing commitments "in true letter and spirit"; expand capacity-building and means of implementation.
- NDC (2022 update): 45% emissions-intensity cut vs 2005 by 2030; ~50% non-fossil installed capacity; extra 2.5–3 Gt CO₂e sink; net zero 2070.
- Under the COP30 arrangement Türkiye hosts and Australia leads negotiations; India has offered to host COP33 (2028).
- **Notebook:** GS3 Environment / GS2 IR.

### Also worth a line (headline-level, not independently verified from PIB text)
- **Ports, Shipping & Waterways:** Sagarmanthan 2026 (3rd edition, New Delhi, 7 Oct, with ORF) — India–EU Green Shipping Corridor, IMEC institutionalisation; Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047 (~₹80 lakh crore investment need).
- **Finance:** FM Nirmala Sitharaman visiting Singapore (9 Oct).

articles.title: India backs a "fair PABS" at the UN pandemic meeting; the Pandemic Agreement still cannot open for signature — International Relations
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** At the UN High-Level Meeting on pandemic prevention, preparedness and response (New York, 25 Sep 2026), India (represented by the Union Health Secretary) said a fair Pathogen Access and Benefit-Sharing (PABS) system is central to the Agreement's credibility and that the political declaration should not prejudge the ongoing PABS talks. The fault line is North–South: high-income countries resist mandatory technology transfer, while developing countries want guaranteed access to vaccines and diagnostics in return for sharing pathogen data. India stresses national sovereignty, domestic financing and digital public infrastructure as a global public good.
**Key facts:** WHO Pandemic Agreement adopted by the WHA on 20 May 2025 (124 in favour, 0 against, 11 abstentions). Article 12 creates PABS via an annex; the Agreement opens for signature only once the annex is adopted (negotiated in an Intergovernmental Working Group). PABS is modelled on the Nagoya Protocol (prior informed consent, mutually agreed terms, benefit sharing). India's COVID-19 record: about 300 million vaccine doses to about 100 countries.
**Notebook:** GS2 – International Relations (global health governance).
**Static anchor:** Mrunal/Shankar IAS – International Organisations (WHO); Environment – CBD & Nagoya Protocol. *Nudge:* add a cross-link from the WHO page to the Nagoya Protocol/ABS note and to the Biological Diversity Act, 2002.

articles.title: Wildlife Week recoveries: dugong reserve, snow leopard safari, vultures and lions — Environment
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** An editorial at the end of Wildlife Week (2–8 Oct) collects India's species-recovery data, a handy case-study bank for Mains. Key policy hook: the Integrated Development of Wildlife Habitats (IDWH) scheme funds recovery programmes for 24 critically endangered species. Bottlenecks: funding skewed to charismatic megafauna, power lines as a leading cause of Great Indian Bustard deaths, and poor assessment data for reptiles, amphibians and invertebrates.
**Key facts:** Asiatic lion 674 (2020) → 891 (2025). Madhya Pradesh vultures 8,397 (2019) → 12,981 (2025). Nilgiri tahr 1,303 (2025) → 1,364 (2026). Dugong: about 270 (158 Palk Bay, 112 Gulf of Mannar; 2026 WII assessment) in a 448.34 sq km Conservation Reserve in Palk Bay; Schedule I of WPA 1972, IUCN Vulnerable. Snow leopard: 718 (first national assessment, 2024), 477 of them in Ladakh. Ladakh has launched India's first high-altitude snow leopard safari (Rumbak, Shang, Uley). *(Figures per The Hindu / Insights digests, 8 Oct.)*
**Notebook:** GS3 – Environment & Biodiversity.
**Static anchor:** Shankar IAS – Biodiversity: Conservation (in situ/ex situ, species recovery programmes); Wildlife Protection Act schedules. *Nudge:* update the species-population table (lion, vulture, tahr, dugong, snow leopard) with the new numbers.

articles.title: Nobel Prize in Chemistry 2026: Henri Kagan and Kenso Soai for chirality and asymmetric catalysis — Science & Technology
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** The prize recognises how small imbalances between mirror-image (left/right-handed) molecules can be amplified, relevant to single-enantiomer drugs (one mirror form may be therapeutic, the other harmful) and to the long-standing puzzle of biological homochirality. Prelims-style questions usually ask "what is the discovery about", not the laureates alone.
**Key facts:** Henri B. Kagan (France; non-linear effects, mid-1980s) and Kenso Soai (Japan; Soai reaction, 1995, an asymmetric autocatalytic reaction). Prize money 12 million SEK, shared. Link to the Physics Nobel 2026 (Halzen, IceCube) covered on 7 Oct.
**Notebook:** GS3 – Science & Technology (basic science, pharma).
**Static anchor:** NCERT Class 11/12 Chemistry – Optical isomerism/stereochemistry. *Nudge:* add a "Nobel 2026" box listing Physics and Chemistry with one-line explainers.

articles.title: Supreme Court issues notice on accessibility in air travel for persons with disabilities — Polity & Governance
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** Per The Hindu (8 Oct), the SC issued notice to the Ministry of Civil Aviation, DGCA, AAI, CISF and the Digi Yatra Foundation on a plea citing gaps such as missing ambulifts, inaccessible in-flight systems and silent airports, and an alleged offloading of a wheelchair user. The petition estimates over 7 million disabled air passengers a year (using the 2011 Census figure of 2.21%). Constitutional hooks: Article 21 (dignity), Article 14, Article 41 (DPSP) and the RPwD Act, 2016 (accessibility provisions). *This is a notice, not a verdict; follow the next hearing.*
**Key facts:** RPwD Act 2016 recognises 21 disabilities; benchmark disability is at least 40%; 4% reservation in government posts. India's domestic air traffic grows about 10–12% a year (per petition).
**Notebook:** GS2 – Polity/Governance (vulnerable sections, judiciary).
**Static anchor:** Laxmikanth – Ch. on Fundamental Rights (Art. 21) and DPSP; Social Justice notes on RPwD Act. *Nudge:* add a PIL case-study line under "judicial activism in welfare".

articles.title: Ministry of Textiles: Development Council for Textile Industry (DCTI) holds first meeting (6 Oct, New Delhi) *(single secondary source citing PIB)*
articles.text:
**What / why it matters:** A consultative council chaired by the Secretary, Textiles, to guide the sector on production and productivity, R&D, exports, raw-material supply, investment, skilling and sustainability; working groups will be formed on priority themes. Reflects institutionalised industry–government consultation.

**Notebook:** GS3 Economy (industry)

articles.title: SEBI (Ministry of Finance regulator): 'Samajh Se Investing Simple' launched under Project Jagrook; SEBI starts official WhatsApp Channel (5 Oct, Panjab University, Chandigarh) *(single source, flagged)*
articles.text:
**What / why it matters:** Investor-awareness push marking World Investor Week; AMFI signed an MoU with the university at the launch. Relevant to financial literacy and investor protection.

**Notebook:** GS3 Economy (capital markets)

articles.title: RBI hikes repo rate 25 bps to 5.50% — first hike since Feb 2023; stance turns "calibrated tightening" — Economy
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** After holding 5.25% for four reviews (125 bps of cuts in 2025), the MPC voted unanimously for a hike. The Governor said inflation and its outlook "are not benign" as last year, and near-term cuts are off the table. Drivers cited: food and fuel inflation with second-round risks, a deficient monsoon (2026 closed at 87% of LPA), crude near US$100/bbl and elevated global yields. A classic supply-shock vs. demand-management debate for Mains.
**Memorize:** Repo 5.50%; SDF 5.25%; MSF and Bank Rate 5.75%; CPI FY27 5.2% (Q2 4.9, Q3 6.0, Q4 5.7); real GDP FY27 7.1%; inflation target 4% ±2%.
**Notebook:** GS3 Economy (Monetary Policy, Inflation).
**Static anchor:** Mrunal Economy pillar "Monetary policy and inflation targeting" / Ramesh Singh, Money & Banking chapter. *Update:* add the 2026 hike cycle to the policy-rate timeline and cross-link to the 87% LPA monsoon note (Geography).

articles.title: Nobel Prize in Physics 2026: Francis Halzen, for building IceCube and opening neutrino astronomy — Science & Technology
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** Announced 6 Oct and reported as a sole award. IceCube is a cubic-kilometre detector in Antarctic ice at the South Pole that records faint light from charged particles made when neutrinos interact. Its results mark the birth of "multi-messenger astrophysics", the same family of ideas behind India's planned INO. Directly useful for the Physics optional (particle physics, astrophysics).
**Memorize:** Halzen first proposed the project in 1988; IceCube completed c. 2011; first high-energy extraterrestrial neutrinos 2013; blazar source evidence 2017–18; Milky Way neutrinos 2023. Neutrinos: neutral, nearly massless, weakly interacting.
**Notebook:** GS3 Sci-Tech (Physics/Space) + Physics optional.
**Static anchor:** Spectrum / NCERT Class 12 Physics (Nuclei) and Shankar IAS "Basic Science: particles". *Update:* add IceCube next to INO (Bodi West Hills, Theni, Tamil Nadu) as a comparison card.

articles.title: Jaishankar's Africa tour: Ghana, Côte d'Ivoire, Ethiopia — science and agriculture MoUs in Accra — International Relations
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** The Ghana leg (6 Oct) covered trade, defence, technology and multilateral engagement, and produced two MoUs: Zoological Survey of India with the University of Ghana, and ICAR with CSIR-Crops Research Institute. It follows PM Modi's July 2025 Ghana visit (first bilateral PM visit in about three decades) and positions India for the AU/ECOWAS outreach.
**Memorize:** Tour = Ghana, Côte d'Ivoire, Ethiopia (Ethiopia hosts the African Union HQ); MoUs = ZSI–Univ. of Ghana, ICAR–CSIR-CRI. Ghana's President Mahama is slated to take the AU chair in 2027 (per one source; verify).
**Notebook:** GS2 International Relations (India–Africa).
**Static anchor:** Shankar IAS / Mrunal IR pillar "India and Africa" (India-Africa Forum Summit, AU's G20 membership 2023). *Update:* add Ghana row to the India-Africa partnership table.

articles.title: Cabinet clears Integrated Transport & Logistics Authority (ITLA) and a ₹10,000 crore SME Growth Fund — Economy (Infrastructure)
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** ITLA is an apex body to prepare a long-term transport master plan across eight domains (roads, railways, ports and shipping, civil aviation, inland waterways, coastal shipping, urban mobility, logistics), appraise and monitor projects of ₹500 crore and above, and run a data repository (reports mention GSTN, FASTag, Vahan data). The SME Growth Fund is a ₹10,000 crore equity fund for growth-stage SMEs, aimed at the "missing middle" between startups and bank credit. Reports describe it as an AIF; its manager and structure were not confirmed.
**Memorize:** ITLA threshold ₹500 crore; 8 transport domains; SME fund ₹10,000 crore (direct equity). Fits PM Gati Shakti and the National Logistics Policy 2022 (logistics cost target to be benchmarked, not memorised).
**Notebook:** GS3 Economy (Infrastructure, MSMEs).
**Static anchor:** Mrunal Economy pillar "Infrastructure and Logistics". *Update:* link ITLA with PM Gati Shakti and NLP 2022 in one flow chart.

articles.title: Great Nicobar: SC won't stay Calcutta HC hearings; "preservation of culture is a fundamental right" — Polity & Governance
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** On 5 Oct a bench of CJI Surya Kant, Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana declined to interfere with the Calcutta HC order upholding maintainability of a PIL alleging Forest Rights Act violations (consent of tribal communities) in the project. Justice Bagchi's oral remark: protecting the Shompen's identity, not forcing integration, is a constitutionally protected right. A live test of development vs tribal rights vs ecology.
**Memorize:** Shompen = PVTG; HC next hearing 25–26 Nov; two earlier NGT proceedings exist; FRA 2006 requires gram sabha consent.
**Notebook:** GS2 Polity/Governance (also GS1 Society, GS3 Environment).
**Static anchor:** Laxmikanth — Fundamental Rights (Arts 21, 29) + Scheduled & Tribal Areas; *Update:* add "Great Nicobar 2026 – culture as a right" under Art 29(1) and link to PVTG list.

articles.title: First international cargo from Bogibeel: Brahmaputra trade route reopens — Economy
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** On 5 Oct Sarbananda Sonowal flagged off barge DLB Patkai (tug Kushal Konwar) carrying 540 MT methanol from APCL, Namrup to Dhaka region via NW-2 and the Indo-Bangladesh Protocol Route. Reported as the first cargo from Upper Assam to a foreign port since 1947; ties to Act East, NE connectivity and Bangladesh relations.
**Memorize:** ~768 km on NW-2, ~1,300 km total; NW-2 = Brahmaputra, Sadiya–Dhubri; NW-1 = Ganga, Prayagraj–Haldia.
**Notebook:** GS3 Economy (Infrastructure/Logistics); GS2 IR (Bangladesh).
**Static anchor:** Ramesh Singh/Shankar — Transport: Inland Waterways; Spectrum Geography — Brahmaputra; *Update:* add 2026 Bogibeel cross-link to the National Waterways list.

articles.title: India–Japan Joint Crediting Mechanism gets its Operational Manual — Environment
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** Launched 30 Sep in New Delhi by Japan's Ambassador and the MoEFCC Secretary. Covers the cycle from Project Idea Note to issuance and authorisation of credits under Article 6.2 of the Paris Agreement. Eligible: green hydrogen, offshore wind, storage-backed renewables, CCUS. Relates to India's Carbon Credit Trading Scheme.
**Memorize:** MoC 7 Aug 2025 → Rules 8 Jun 2026 → Manual 30 Sep 2026; India NDC: 45% intensity cut by 2030, net zero 2070.
**Notebook:** GS3 Environment (also GS2 IR – Japan).
**Static anchor:** Shankar IAS — Climate Change: Paris Agreement & carbon markets; *Update:* add JCM as a worked Article 6.2 example next to CCTS.

articles.title: India's supercomputing ecosystem: 40 indigenous systems, ~68 PF — Science & Technology
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** Under the National Supercomputing Mission (2015; ~₹4,500 cr; DST + MeitY; C-DAC and IISc), 40 systems with ~68 petaflops are deployed, using indigenous Rudra servers and Trinetra interconnects (100/200 Gbps). Mains lens: imported CPUs/GPUs remain the self-reliance gap.
**Memorize:** 40 systems / 68 PF; PARAM Rudra; Trinetra-A/B; uses: weather, drug screening, genomics, seismic imaging.
**Notebook:** GS3 Science & Technology.
**Static anchor:** Spectrum/Shankar S&T — Computing & Supercomputers (PARAM Siddhi, Pratyush); *Update:* add NSM progress figures; cross-link to semiconductor mission.

articles.title: Union Cabinet (infrastructure & logistics planning): Integrated Transport and Logistics Authority (ITLA) approved as a Special Purpose Vehicle (6 Oct)
articles.text:
**What / why it matters:** Cabinet approved a new body to end fragmented planning across transport agencies. It is meant to bring roads, railways, ports, shipping, civil aviation, inland waterways, coastal shipping, urban mobility and logistics under one planning, appraisal and monitoring lens — directly relevant to PM Gati Shakti-style multimodal integration and the National Logistics Policy, 2022.

**Key facts:**
- Prepares a **National Transport Master Plan** with a 10+ year horizon; checks sectoral and annual plans for consistency and multimodal integration.
- **Technical appraisal and monitoring of projects costing ₹500 crore or above.**
- Builds a **National Transport Data Repository** integrating GSTN, FASTag, Vahan and GPS datasets.
- Advises on updating the **National Logistics Policy, 2022**; supports capacity building and research.
- Administrative ministry and head of ITLA were not stated in the reports retrieved.

**Notebook:** GS3 Economy (Infrastructure & Logistics); GS2 Governance (institutional design).

articles.title: Union Cabinet (MSME / finance): ₹10,000 crore government commitment to the SME Growth Fund (SGF) (6 Oct)
articles.text:
**What / why it matters:** Addresses the gap in *growth-stage equity* for small and medium enterprises that already have established operations but cannot get long-term equity from banks. Announced in Union Budget 2026-27; Cabinet has now cleared the commitment.

**Key facts:**
- Structured as an **Alternative Investment Fund (AIF)**; government's aggregate commitment ₹10,000 crore.
- **Direct equity investments** for capacity expansion, technology adoption, overseas market entry and acquisitions.
- **Majority of allocation to small and medium manufacturing enterprises**; priority to industrial clusters in **Tier-II and Tier-III cities**.
- Managing entity / ministry not named in the retrieved reports (not verified; do not assume SIDBI).

**Notebook:** GS3 Economy (MSMEs, capital formation, manufacturing).

### Scheme-in-focus: **SME Growth Fund (SGF)**
- **Ministry:** Union Cabinet decision, Budget 2026-27 announcement (implementing agency not verified).
- **Objective:** Provide patient growth equity to scale SMEs into "future global champions".
- **Key features:** AIF route; ₹10,000 crore government commitment; direct equity; manufacturing-heavy allocation; Tier-II/III cluster priority.
- **Beneficiaries:** Viable, scalable small and medium enterprises, especially manufacturers.
- **Significance:** Fills the missing-middle financing gap, supports Make in India and regional job creation.

articles.title: Ministry of Environment, Forest & Climate Change: India–Japan Joint Crediting Mechanism (JCM) — Operational Manual launched (30 Sep, reported 6 Oct)
articles.text:
**What / why it matters:** The JCM is a bilateral carbon-crediting arrangement under **Article 6.2 of the Paris Agreement**, letting Japan finance low-carbon projects in India and take part of the resulting credits. The Operational Manual covers the full project cycle — from Project Idea Note to credit issuance — and makes India's first Article 6.2 framework practically usable.

**Key facts:**
- Memorandum of Cooperation: **7 August 2025**; Rules of Implementation adopted **8 June 2026**; Operational Manual: **30 September 2026**.
- Targets advanced low-carbon technologies and climate-finance mobilisation.
- Source note: dates are from a secondary PIB-summary site; Carbon Pulse independently reported the rules' adoption in June 2026 (PIB text not retrieved).

**Notebook:** GS3 Environment (carbon markets, climate finance); GS2 International Relations (Japan).

articles.title: Swiss President Parmelin's state visit: Modi pitches "$100 billion and 10 lakh jobs" under India–EFTA TEPA — International Relations
articles.text:
**Exam angle.** Swiss President Guy Parmelin began a three-day state visit on 5 Oct 2026 (talks at Hyderabad House, Rajghat tribute). The summit is the first big political push on the India–EFTA TEPA after it came into force, with MoUs including migration and mobility, plus talk of cooperation in S&T, nuclear energy, transport and defence. Prelims angle: what EFTA is and who is in it. Mains angle: FTAs with non-EU European blocs, investment-linked trade deals, mobility provisions.
**Memorise.**
- TEPA signed 10 Mar 2024; in force 1 Oct 2025; India's first FTA with a European economic bloc (Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, Switzerland).
- Target: $100 billion investment and 10 lakh (1 million) direct jobs in India over 15 years.
- Switzerland is the biggest EFTA trade and investment partner of India; Swiss focus sectors: biotech, life sciences, banking, insurance, food processing, sustainability.
- Second India–EFTA Prosperity Summit follows; reports give 7 Oct and 8 Oct (sources differ).
- Flag: one report says TEPA came into force in "October 2026"; this is wrong, it was 1 Oct 2025.

**Notebook:** GS2 IR.
**Static anchor:** Mrunal IR pillar, "India and Europe / FTAs"; Shankar IAS "Regional groupings: EFTA". *Nudge:* add EFTA to your regional-groupings sheet (members, non-EU status, TEPA) and cross-link to the India–NZ FTA (20 Oct) entry.

articles.title: IWC-70 in Hobart: India reaffirms science-based cetacean conservation as the 1946 whaling convention turns 80 — Environment
articles.text:
**Exam angle.** The International Whaling Commission's 70th meeting ran 28 Sept–2 Oct 2026 in Hobart, Australia, marking 80 years of the International Convention for the Regulation of Whaling. India stressed science-based conservation and better data on cetacean status, distribution and breeding, and pointed to the Wildlife (Protection) Act, marine protected areas and Project Dolphin. Typical Prelims "statement" fodder on international bodies.
**Memorise.**
- IWC: set up under the ICRW, 1946 (Washington); commercial-whaling moratorium in effect since 1986; not a UN agency.
- India joined in 1981 and supports conservation, not whaling.
- India's tools: WPA 1972 (highest protection for cetaceans), Project Dolphin, marine protected areas.
- Arabian Sea humpback whale is among the species flagged for priority action.
- Related: Indian Ocean Whale Sanctuary (1979) and Southern Ocean Sanctuary (1994), from general knowledge, not from today's reports.

**Notebook:** GS3 Environment.
**Static anchor:** Shankar IAS "International conventions and bodies: IWC, CITES, CMS"; Mrunal Environment pillar, "Marine conservation". *Nudge:* add IWC to your conventions table (year, HQ, India's status) and cross-link to the Buxa/GIB conservation entries.

articles.title: Delhi High Court: a valid visa is not a right of entry — Polity & Governance
articles.text:
**Exam angle.** On 1 Oct 2026 Justice Amit Mahajan dismissed a Turkmenistan national's plea after she was denied entry, holding that visa issue and permission to enter are separate and officers keep discretion on grounds like national security, foreign policy and document mismatches. A neat peg for the citizen–alien distinction in fundamental rights and the executive's sovereign power over entry.
**Memorise.**
- Visa gives permission to apply for entry; the final decision rests with the immigration officer.
- Petition failed due to mismatched personal details and no business documents for the stated purpose.
- Constitutional frame: Article 21 (and 14) apply to all "persons"; Article 19 freedoms, including residence and settlement, are for citizens only.
- Reported statutes: the court spoke of the statutory immigration framework; the exact Act cited was not confirmed in my sources.

**Notebook:** GS2 Polity.
**Static anchor:** Laxmikanth "Fundamental Rights" and "Citizenship". *Nudge:* add a "rights of persons vs citizens" table and this case as a one-line example.

articles.title: Department of Pharmaceuticals (Ministry of Chemicals & Fertilizers): PRIP scheme opens a "New Discovery Track" — up to ₹50 crore per project (announced 30 Sep–1 Oct)
articles.text:
### Scheme-in-focus: **PRIP — Promotion of Research and Innovation in Pharma MedTech**
- **Ministry:** Chemicals & Fertilizers (Department of Pharmaceuticals). Total outlay about ₹5,000 crore.
- **Objective:** Move India from generics towards innovation-led drug and medtech R&D by bridging funding gaps.
- **Key features:** (i) Early Stage track: up to ₹5 crore (TRL 1–3 to 5). (ii) Later Stage track: up to ₹100 crore at 35% of project cost (TRL 4–6). (iii) **New Discovery Track:** up to ₹50 crore per company/project/portfolio for new chemical and new biological entities at TRL 1–3, with at least 25% co-funding by institutional investors; carries projects up to TRL 6. (iv) Second application call announced.
- **Beneficiaries:** Start-ups and MSMEs (Discovery Track); companies and academia under other tracks.
- **Coverage so far:** the first call approved 41 projects, about ₹1,600 crore of assistance.
- **Significance:** Targets the earliest, riskiest stage of drug discovery and crowds in private capital. It complements PLI for pharma and bulk-drug parks and supports Viksit Bharat self-reliance in medicines.

**Notebook:** GS3 Sci-Tech/Economy; GS2 Health.

## Also worth a line (headline-level — not independently verified from PIB text)
- Ministry of Finance's Monthly Economic Review reportedly projects Q2 FY27 GDP growth near 7.3% after 7.8% in Q1; confirm figures on PIB before using.
- BharatNet: Maharashtra cabinet earlier approved Mahanet Digital Infrastructure Ltd (MDIL), an SPV, for the revamped BharatNet programme; a reported Digital Bharat Nidhi agreement with ₹10,520 crore for 28,237 Gram Panchayats could not be verified.

articles.title: India–Russia: the MEA Consultative Committee lays out connectivity, energy and trade — International Relations
articles.text:
**Exam angle.** The Parliamentary Consultative Committee on External Affairs reviewed ties with Russia on 3 Oct 2026. India repeated that it will help "bring the war to an end", building on PM Modi's line to Putin at the SCO summit in Bishkek (31 Aug): "endless war must now give way to an end of war". The static-rich part is connectivity: the Chennai–Vladivostok corridor, the INSTC and the Northern Sea Route. New sub-development only; the BRICS and SCO coverage from earlier this month is not repeated.
**Memorise.**
- Corridors: Chennai–Vladivostok (maritime), INSTC (multi-modal via Iran and the Caspian, avoids Suez), Northern Sea Route (Russian Arctic coast).
- Trade push in seven sectors: auto, pharma, food, marine products, engineering goods, chemicals, textiles.
- Progress reported toward an India–Eurasian Economic Union FTA.
- Ukraine's FM Sybiha called India's proposal "the most comprehensive" of four peace proposals (reported by ANI).

**Notebook:** GS2 IR.
**Static anchor:** Mrunal IR pillar, "India–Russia"; Shankar IAS / Spectrum "Foreign Policy". *Nudge:* add a "connectivity corridors" box (INSTC, Chennai–Vladivostok, NSR, IMEC, Chabahar) and cross-link it to the Bhutan LoC and Kaliningrad entries.

articles.title: First release of captive-bred Great Indian Bustards: two males enter the wild in Jaisalmer — Environment
articles.text:
**Exam angle.** Union Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav and the Wildlife Institute of India released two captive-bred male GIBs near Jaisalmer on 4 Oct 2026, after rewilding training. It is the first test of whether ex situ breeding can feed in situ recovery of a Critically Endangered, power-line-vulnerable species. Mains hook: limits of captive breeding, habitat and infrastructure conflict (overhead lines).
**Memorise.**
- Two males, tagged for monitoring, released into a restricted-to-humans enclosure.
- Run by WII with the Rajasthan Forest Department; breeding centres at Sam and Ramdevra (Jaisalmer).
- Globally, captive-bred bustard survival is about 48%, ANI reports; about 98 chicks bred so far.
- GIB: IUCN Critically Endangered; Schedule I, WPA 1972; Rajasthan's state bird; Desert National Park and Thar are its core range.
- Supreme Court (2021) directions on power lines; priority area about 14,013 sq km (as reported).
- Flag: sources differ on how many birds were planned (10 vs 2); only the two actually released are used here.

**Notebook:** GS3 Environment.
**Static anchor:** Shankar IAS "Biodiversity: species in news"; Mrunal Environment pillar, "Conservation: in situ vs ex situ". *Nudge:* add a GIB row to the species card; cross-link to the Buxa tigress item (rewilding vs reintroduction).

articles.title: Poompuhar's seabed gives up a Mediterranean wine jar — Ancient History / Art & Culture
articles.text:
**Exam angle.** The third phase of underwater exploration at Poompuhar (Kaveripoompattinam), by the Tamil Nadu State Department of Archaeology with the Indian Maritime University, ended on 22 Sept 2026. The finds corroborate Sangam-age maritime trade with West Asia and the Mediterranean and show a submerged city. A natural fit for GS1 (Sangam Age, Indo-Roman trade) and Prelims "ports" questions.
**Memorise.**
- A West Asian torpedo-jar fragment (30–35 cm), used to carry wine and olive oil.
- Over 250 ceramic pieces, four terracotta ring wells; read as a buried palaeochannel swallowed by the sea (about 4th–5th century CE).
- Tools: side-scan sonar, sub-bottom profiler, multibeam, ROVs.
- Poompuhar = Chola port at the Cauvery mouth; other sites to pair: Arikamedu, Alagankulam, Muziris/Pattanam.

**Notebook:** GS1 Ancient History and Art & Culture.
**Static anchor:** NCERT Old (R.S. Sharma) "Sangam age"; Nitin Singhania "Ancient trade". *Nudge:* update your ports table (Poompuhar–Chola, Korkai–Pandya, Muziris and Tondi–Chera) with this find.

articles.title: Monsoon 2026 closes at 87% of LPA — the driest since 2015, and the east is the worst hit — Geography
articles.text:
**Exam angle.** IMD's season summary (30 Sept): 759.4 mm, 87% of LPA, 4th lowest since 2001. The new angle versus the drought-watch item of 25 Sept is the full-season map: Central India was normal, while East/North-East and the South Peninsula were badly short. A model Mains case for El Niño years and regional variation.
**Memorise.**
- Seasonal: 759.4 mm = 87% of LPA (the IMD 'deficient' band is below 90%).
- East and North-East India 74% (lowest since 1901); South Peninsula 76%; North-West 94%; Central 97%.
- Monthly: June 65%, July 101%, August 84%, September 92%.
- Kerala onset 4 June (3 days late); withdrawal began 19 Sept; 17 of 36 subdivisions deficient, only Odisha in excess.
- Strong El Niño influence reported.

**Notebook:** GS1 Geography.
**Static anchor:** NCERT Class XI "India: Physical Environment", Ch. 4 Climate; Mrunal Geography pillar, "Monsoon mechanism". *Nudge:* add a "monsoon 2026" data box to your El Niño and IOD notes.

articles.title: Ministry of Environment, Forest & Climate Change: Two male Great Indian Bustards released into the wild at Desert National Park, Jaisalmer (4 Oct) *(UPDATE — the 3 Oct briefing covered the process being initiated; what is new is the actual first release of two captive-bred males.)*
articles.text:
- **What:** PIB: the Union Environment Minister released **two male** Great Indian Bustards (GIBs) into the wild at Desert National Park — the first actual release in the recovery programme, culminating about ten years of effort (Project GIB, 2016).
- **Why it matters:** Moves from ex-situ breeding to in-situ rewilding; post-release survival (power lines, predators, habitat loss) will decide if the programme works. See the 3 Oct note for the programme background (captive breeding since 2019, "jump-start" egg-swap technique, rewilding tunnel).
- **Static link:** GIB — IUCN *Critically Endangered*, Schedule I WPA 1972, CMS Appendix I, Rajasthan's State bird.
- **Notebook:** GS3 Environment (species conservation).

articles.title: Ministry of Skill Development & Entrepreneurship: PM-SETU completes one year — PIB Backgrounder "Transforming India's ITIs" (3 Oct) *(UPDATE — scheme covered 8 Sep; the one-year stocktake figures could not be retrieved, so only verified scheme facts are given.)*
articles.text:
### Scheme-in-focus: **PM-SETU (Pradhan Mantri Skilling and Employability Transformation through Upgraded ITIs)**
- **Ministry:** MSDE. **Launched:** 4 Oct 2025 (Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi). **Outlay:** ₹60,000 crore.
- **Objective:** Modernise **1,000 government ITIs** into industry-aligned institutions.
- **Key features:** (i) **Hub-and-spoke** — 200 hub ITIs + 800 spoke ITIs (about 4 spokes per hub); (ii) hubs have innovation centres, trainer development, production units, placement support; (iii) **government-owned, industry-managed** with Anchor Industry Partners running clusters; (iv) co-financing by the **World Bank and Asian Development Bank**.
- **Significance:** Addresses skill-mismatch and youth employability; a model of industry-led public-institution governance. **Notebook:** GS2 Governance (skilling) / GS3 Economy (employment).

## Also worth a line (3–4 Oct 2026, headline-level — details not independently verified)
- **NITI Aayog / Vice-President's Secretariat:** 5th **Kautilya Economic Conclave**, New Delhi — Vice-President C. P. Radhakrishnan gave the inaugural address; NITI Aayog member Rajiv Gauba called for a shift to **light-touch, risk-proportionate regulation** (ties to the "next-generation reforms"/deregulation theme).
- **PMO:** PM congratulated Indian athletes after multiple Asian Games medals (men's hockey and cricket golds retained; golds for Aman Sehrawat, Pranavi Sharath Urs, Kumkum Anil Mohod).
- **Ministry of Jal Shakti:** "Jal Arpan" observed in 1,850+ Gram Panchayats during Gandhi Jayanti Special Gram Sabhas.
- **Ministry of Cooperation:** Amit Shah addressed the Gaupalak Sammelan, Bhopal.

articles.title: Rabi MSPs for 2027-28: wheat up only ₹25 to ₹2,610, while pulses and oilseeds get the bigger hikes — Agriculture
articles.text:
**Exam angle.** The CCEA (30 Sept 2026) approved MSPs for six rabi crops. The hike is lopsided: the cereal (wheat) gets a small raise and the oilseeds and pulses get large ones. That fits the policy push to cut edible-oil and pulse imports and shift area away from wheat. It is a good Mains hook on MSP design and cropping-pattern signals.
**Memorise.**
- Wheat ₹2,610 (+₹25; expected return ~106%, the highest).
- Barley ₹2,286 (+₹136).
- Gram ₹5,958 (+₹83).
- Masur ₹7,390 (+₹390).
- Rapeseed-mustard ₹6,613 (+₹413).
- Safflower ₹7,215 (+₹675, the largest absolute rise and the lowest return, ~50%).
- Policy basis: MSP is set at at least 1.5× the all-India weighted average cost of production (A2+FL).
- CACP recommends, CCEA decides.

**Notebook:** GS3 Agriculture.
**Static anchor:** Mrunal Agriculture pillar, "MSP, procurement & CACP"; Shankar IAS "Agriculture – Pricing". *Nudge:* add a one-line row to your MSP card: "Rabi 2027-28: wheat ₹2,610; safflower ₹7,215". Cross-link to the edible-oil duty cut (25 Sept) and the pulses self-reliance mission.

articles.title: Places in News — Kaliningrad: Putin's "all weapons" warning — Geography
articles.text:
**Exam angle.** On 1 Oct 2026 at the Valdai Forum Putin said Russia would use "all the weapons at our country's disposal" if Kaliningrad were attacked. Reports say NATO also received a Russian diplomatic note on a possible nuclear response if the exclave is cut off. Kaliningrad's location, as a non-contiguous Russian territory on the Baltic between Poland and Lithuania, is what makes it a standing flashpoint. Map-based questions are likely.
**Memorise.**
- Kaliningrad Oblast: Russian exclave on the Baltic coast between Poland and Lithuania, with no land link to mainland Russia.
- Baltic Fleet HQ at Baltiysk.
- The Suwałki Gap (the Poland–Lithuania land strip between Kaliningrad and Belarus) is the NATO-side pressure point.
- NATO chief Rutte responded that the alliance is defensive.

**Notebook:** GS1 Geography (Places in News); links to GS2 IR (Russia–NATO).
**Static anchor:** Spectrum / NCERT "World map – Europe & Baltic"; Mrunal "World Geography – Baltic Sea". *Nudge:* add Kaliningrad, the Suwałki Gap, Baltiysk and the Baltic states to your Europe map sheet.

articles.title: Ministry of Environment, Forest & Climate Change: Process begins for release of captive-bred Great Indian Bustards into the wild at Desert National Park, Jaisalmer (3 Oct)
articles.text:
- **What:** PIB reports that, "in culmination of 10 years of dedicated efforts", Union Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav and the Rajasthan Chief Minister initiated the process for release of captive-bred Great Indian Bustards (GIBs) into the wild at Desert National Park, Jaisalmer. Press reports put the release schedule at 3 Oct (Ramdevra) and 4 Oct (Sudasari area), with ten birds having completed "rewilding" training in a specially designed tunnel; the exact number for the first release is to be fixed after assessment by Wildlife Institute of India (WII) scientists.
- **Why it matters:** This is the first move from *ex-situ* conservation breeding to *in-situ* rewilding for one of India's most threatened birds. It tests whether captive-bred birds can survive predation, power lines and habitat loss — the three main killers of the species. It also marks a shift from species-specific work to an **ecosystem (grassland) approach**: the National Board for Wildlife standing committee recently decided to fold Lesser Florican and Bengal Florican into the bustard recovery programme.
- **Key facts:** Project GIB launched **2016**; captive breeding began **2019**; first captive-bred chick **March 2023**; rewilding training since **2025**. Release site originally planned in Kachchh (Gujarat) but Thar chosen as native habitat. Post-release tracking will study behaviour and survival. "Jump-start" technique: fertile captive eggs swapped with infertile wild eggs so wild females incubate and rear the chicks. Other candidate grasslands named: MP, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh.
- **Static link (standard knowledge):** GIB is Rajasthan's State bird, IUCN *Critically Endangered*, Schedule I of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, and listed in CMS Appendix I; Desert National Park (Jaisalmer–Barmer) is its main stronghold.
- **Notebook:** GS3 Environment (species conservation, ex-situ vs in-situ, grasslands, renewable-energy vs biodiversity conflict).

articles.title: Rajasthan High Court warns Jaipur's Walled City could lose World Heritage status — Art & Culture
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** In a suo motu case, the Rajasthan HC (order of 26 Sep 2026) said the Walled City faces a "serious risk" if remedial action is not taken by December 2026. It ordered a survey of unauthorised construction (two weeks), an affidavit on safeguards (four weeks), and a phase-wise action plan, and asked why officials should not face action. UNESCO has flagged redevelopment in the core and buffer zones; the conservation report is due in December 2026 and review is expected at the 2027 World Heritage Committee session (per Outlook Traveller, March 2026).
**Memorize:** Jaipur Walled City inscribed 2019 (founded 1727). The World Heritage Committee decides on the List of World Heritage in Danger and on deletion. Tools: Heritage Impact Assessment, buffer zone, Reactive Monitoring. Only a handful of sites have ever been delisted globally.
**Notebook:** GS1 Art & Culture (Heritage conservation); GS2 Polity (judicial activism).
**Static anchor:** Nitin Singhania *Art & Culture* — UNESCO sites; NCERT *Class 11 An Introduction to Indian Art*. **Nudge:** add Jaipur to a "WH sites under UNESCO scrutiny" list with Hampi and Ahmedabad as comparators; cross-link to the Ancient Monuments Act (AMASR Act 1958/2010).
*(Note: this is a follow-up on heritage, not a repeat of the 24 Sep UNESCO Tentative List story.)*

articles.title: Supreme Court: no total firecracker ban, no 24-hour bursting — time-limited use is the middle path — Polity & Governance
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** A clean case of the Court balancing fundamental rights against each other: religious and cultural practice (Art. 25) on one side, and health and a clean environment (Art. 21) on the other. It is a strong Mains example of judicial balancing and of the Court as environmental regulator.
**Memorise:** ***Arjun Gopal v. Union of India*** (W.P.(C) 728/2015), bench of **Justices M.M. Sundresh and Augustine George Masih**. The Court said it would not agree to a **total ban** and would not allow **unrestricted use**, and signalled **specified bursting hours** and limits on cracker types during festivals. It approved manufacture of **new-generation joint (series) crackers** subject to conditions (shell size and quantity limits, intervals between bursts) based on **CSIR-NEERI** specifications. **Barium** content in **Generation-2 green crackers** is being tested in **Delhi, Bhopal, Kolkata and Chennai**; the decision is **deferred to 15 Oct 2026**. Delhi-NCR restrictions run in the separate **M.C. Mehta** proceedings. Constitutional hooks: **Art. 21** (health, clean environment), **Art. 25(1)** (subject to public order, morality, health).
**Notebook:** GS2 – Polity (Judiciary; Fundamental Rights); GS3 – Environment.
**Static anchor:** Laxmikanth, *Fundamental Rights → Art. 21 and Art. 25*. *Nudge:* add "No total ban; time-bound use; barium test decision 15 Oct 2026" under your Art. 21 environmental-rights case list, and cross-link to the GRAP item above.

articles.title: Ministry of Mines: Auction of two offshore mineral blocks in the Andaman Sea launched (1 Oct)
articles.text:
India's first offshore-mineral auction attempt in 2024 (13 blocks) was cancelled; this is a fresh round of two blocks under composite licences (exploration + mining), under the Offshore Areas Mineral (Development & Regulation) Act, 2002 and Offshore Areas Mineral Auction Rules, 2024 (amended 2026).

- Blocks (per reports): **West Sewell Ridge-01** (~1,000 sq km, off Great Nicobar) and **Sewell Rise-01** (~632 sq km); polymetallic nodules/crusts — cobalt, copper, manganese, nickel.
- Rule change (24 Sep 2026): minimum technically-qualified bidders for a first-attempt auction cut from **three to two**, to reduce cancellation risk.
- Significance: critical-mineral security (EV batteries, renewables), Blue Economy, EEZ resource use alongside ISA/UNCLOS frameworks.

**Notebook: GS3 Economy (Mining, Critical Minerals) / GS1 Geography (Oceanic resources).**

articles.title: Places in News: Vasundhara Tal (Chamoli) gets Uttarakhand's first glacial-lake early-warning system — Geography
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** GLOF risk in the Himalaya is a recurring Geography and Disaster Management theme. This item moves it from mapping lakes to instrumenting them. Pair it with the Chamoli disaster of Feb 2021 and the Sikkim South Lhonak GLOF of Oct 2023.
**Memorise:** Installation runs from **29 Sept to 15 Oct 2026**. It was flagged off by Chief Secretary **Anand Bardhan** and is coordinated by the **USDMA**. Other agencies: **Wadia Institute of Himalayan Geology (Dehradun)**, **CBRI (Roorkee)**, **SDRF, NDRF and ITBP**. Equipment:
- water-level sensors
- automatic weather stations (temperature, pressure)
- snow-depth sensors
- **eight sub-surface temperature probes**
- satellite links for real-time alerts

Uttarakhand has **344 glacial lakes**, of which **13 are high-risk** (2023 data): **Pithoragarh 6, Chamoli 4, and one each in Bageshwar, Tehri Garhwal and Uttarkashi**. Vasundhara Tal is a **pilot**, and similar systems are planned for other lakes.
**Notebook:** GS1 – Geography (Glacial landforms; Places in News); GS3 – Disaster Management.
**Static anchor:** NCERT Class 11 *India: Physical Environment*, ch. *Natural Hazards and Disasters*; NCERT Class 11 *Fundamentals of Physical Geography*, ch. *Landforms and their Evolution* (glaciers, moraines). *Nudge:* mark Vasundhara Tal (Chamoli) and the Pithoragarh cluster on your Uttarakhand map, and add "instrumented EWS (2026)" to your NDMA GLOF-mitigation note.

articles.title: Ministry of Steel: Steel Industry Safety Council (SISC) set up as an apex safety body, backed by a Steel Industry Safety Directorate (28–30 Sep)
The Collegium recommends three High Court Chief Justices for the Supreme Court — Polity & Governance
articles.text:
**Exam angle:** This is the first batch of elevations since Parliament raised the Court's strength to 38. It also brings the appointment machinery back into focus: the Judges Cases, the Memorandum of Procedure, seniority and diversity.
**Memorise:** On **28 Sept 2026** the Collegium (**CJI Surya Kant** with Justices Vikram Nath, B.V. Nagarathna, M.M. Sundresh and P.S. Narasimha) recommended **Justice Sunita Agarwal** (CJ, Gujarat HC; parent HC Allahabad), **Justice D.K. Upadhyaya** (CJ, Delhi HC; from Allahabad) and **Justice Aparesh Kumar Singh** (CJ, Telangana HC; parent HC Jharkhand). The SC's working strength is **34 against a sanctioned 38**. If these three are appointed, it becomes **37 with one vacancy**. The strength went from 34 to 38 (CJI + 37) through the **Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Act, 2026**, which got presidential assent on 12 Aug 2026 and replaced the May 2026 Ordinance. Justice Agarwal would make **three women judges** on the SC. None of the three is in line to become CJI. *Mains line:* "Adding benches only helps if appointments keep pace. Sanctioned strength means little without timely elevations."
**Notebook:** GS2 – Polity (Judiciary).
**Static anchor:** Laxmikanth, *Supreme Court* chapter → Composition (Art. 124(1): Parliament fixes the number by law) and Appointment of Judges (the Judges Cases). *Nudge:* change "34" to "38 (2026 Amendment Act)" in your notes and add this batch as a live example beside the Second/Third/Fourth Judges Cases.

articles.title: Jaishankar's UNGA-81 statement: the Indus Waters Treaty goes on the UN record, and India co-founds a shipping-safety group — International Relations
articles.text:
**What's new since the 21 Sept preview:** India delivered its national statement on **26 September 2026**. Two things in it are new for your notes. India defended keeping the **Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) in abeyance** from the UNGA podium. India also joined **Liberia** and about two dozen partners to launch a **Group of Friends on the Safety and Security of Shipping and Seafarers**.

**Exam angle:** This is India's first statement at the General Assembly that ties a water treaty directly to cross-border terrorism. The line was that "friendship and goodwill cannot co-exist with terrorism", and that understandings premised on good faith "will naturally be called into question". For Mains, use it on how far treaty obligations stand when there is a security threat (IR / GS2). The shipping group adds to India's maritime-security material alongside the Red Sea attacks, SAGAR/MAHASAGAR and the IMO.

**Facts to memorise:**
- Speech: 26 Sept 2026, 81st UNGA General Debate. Lines to quote: "Our right to defend ourselves against terrorism will be exercised". He called Pakistan a "serial practitioner of terrorism".
- IWT stays **in abeyance** (in place since April 2025, after Pahalgam) "until Pakistan … credibly and irrevocably ends its support for cross-border … terrorism".
- **IWT basics:** signed **1960, Karachi**, by **Nehru and Ayub Khan**, with the **World Bank** as a signatory. **Eastern rivers** (Ravi, Beas, Sutlej) go to India. **Western rivers** (Indus, Jhelum, Chenab) go to Pakistan, and India has limited non-consumptive uses such as run-of-river hydro. Disputes pass through the **Permanent Indus Commission**, then a Neutral Expert, then a Court of Arbitration.
- Shipping: "the targeting of commercial shipping and seafarers … is simply unacceptable". **Liberia** is one of the world's largest flag-registries, so a flag state is co-leading the group.
- Other lines from the speech: the "**4F crisis**" in the Global South (food, fuel, fertiliser, finance); "endless war must give way to an end to war" (on Ukraine).

**Destination notebook:** GS2 — IR (India–Pakistan; Important international groupings). GS3 link: water security.

**Static anchor:** Your GS2 India–Neighbourhood file (India–Pakistan → IWT). Cross-link to *Spectrum / NCERT Geography — Indus river system*. **Nudge:** add a box showing "IWT: Eastern vs Western rivers + three-tier dispute ladder", and link it to the 21 Sept UNGA card.

articles.title: Places in News: Tigray — TPLF seizes Mekelle, Axum and Shire airports, and the Pretoria peace deal is fraying — Geography
articles.text:
**Headline:** From **23 September 2026** forces of the **Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF)** seized the **Mekelle, Axum and Shire** airports and announced a "defensive war". **Ethiopian Airlines suspended flights** to all three. Fighting has spread into **Amhara and Afar**. A seven-group anti-government alliance announced on 21 September includes **Fano** militias and the **Oromo Liberation Army**, and there are reports of Eritrean support.

**Exam angle:** This is a Places-in-News map drill for the **Horn of Africa**, which sits next to the **Bab el-Mandeb** and the Red Sea shipping route. India has a direct stake: Ethiopia is a **BRICS member (since 1 Jan 2024)**, it hosts the **African Union HQ (Addis Ababa)**, and it is a major destination for Indian investment and lines of credit. The **Pretoria Agreement (Nov 2022)**, brokered by the AU, ended a war that the AU estimates killed about **6 lakh** people.

**Facts to memorise:**
- **Landlocked** since **Eritrea's independence (1993)**. Six neighbours: **Eritrea, Djibouti, Somalia, Kenya, South Sudan, Sudan**. Most trade goes through **Djibouti**.
- **Lake Tana** is the source of the **Blue Nile (Abay)**. **GERD** is on the Blue Nile. Ethiopia is called the "water tower of East Africa".
- **Danakil Depression (Afar)**, part of the **Great Rift Valley**, is one of the hottest and lowest places on Earth. The **Tekeze** river forms part of the Tigray–Amhara boundary zone.
- **Axum** (Aksum) was the seat of the ancient Aksumite kingdom and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. **Mekelle** is Tigray's capital.

**Destination notebook:** GS1 — Geography (Places in News: Africa). GS2 link: India–Africa.

**Static anchor:** *NCERT Class XI "Fundamentals of Physical Geography" — plate tectonics / rift valleys*; atlas work on the Horn of Africa. **Nudge:** mark Mekelle, Axum, Shire, Lake Tana, the Danakil Depression and Djibouti port on your Africa blank map, and cross-link to the 13 Sept Perim Island / Bab el-Mandeb card.

articles.title: Election Commission of India: Full Commission decides on SIR document collection, ECINet audit and new transparency rules; claims deadlines extended for Delhi and Maharashtra
articles.text:
On **26 September 2026**, the full Commission met: CEC **Gyanesh Kumar** and Election Commissioners **S.S. Sandhu** and **Vivek Joshi**. It issued a set of decisions on the ongoing **Special Intensive Revision (SIR)** of electoral rolls. The meeting followed press reports of dissent inside the Commission. The ECI says every SIR decision, starting with the **24 June 2025** order that began the exercise, was **unanimous**.

**Why it matters:** This is a live case study in how a multi-member constitutional body governs itself under **Article 324**. It connects to voter-roll integrity, the risk of exclusion, and the ECI's own internal procedures. All three are standard GS2 Mains themes.

**Key decisions**
- **Doorstep collection:** For "unmapped" electors, **BLOs will collect documents at home** and upload them to **ECINet** for the ERO to decide. A hearing will be held only in exceptional cases, **preferably online**, and a family member can represent the elector.
- **Inclusion:** DEOs must set up **help desks and special camps** for the homeless, labourers and economically weaker voters.
- **Form 6:** The Commission noted that the Supreme Court has upheld the Form 6 declaration used during SIR. Outside SIR periods, the regular forms under the **Registration of Electors Rules, 1960** apply.
- **ECINet audit:** A committee headed by the **Senior Deputy Election Commissioner**, with an **independent IIT/IIIT expert**, will check whether ECINet complies with electoral law and rules.
- **Deadlines extended:** **Delhi**: claims and objections until **30 October 2026**, disposal until **30 November**. **Maharashtra**: claims and objections until **12 October**, disposal until **10 November**.
- **Internal governance:** Agendas will be circulated before Commission meetings and minutes issued afterwards. APARs must be completed by **31 December** each year, and officers need prior approval for foreign trips.
- According to the release, **SIR has been completed in 20 States/UTs**.

**Destination notebook:** GS2 — Polity (ECI, Article 324, electoral rolls, RP Act 1950).

articles.title: Ministry of Commerce & Industry: Interest-free working capital of ₹50,000 per barn for FCV tobacco farmers in Andhra Pradesh
articles.text:
On **25 September 2026**, the Centre approved an **Interest-Free Working Capital Assistance Scheme** for **Flue-Cured Virginia (FCV) tobacco** growers in **Andhra Pradesh**. The government linked the move to weaker global demand, geopolitical developments and shifts in international trade. About **100 million kg** of FCV tobacco had been auctioned in the **2025-26 season**, which opened on **25 March 2026**.

**Why it matters:** This is a textbook conflict for Mains. Farm-income distress in a crop whose exports earn foreign exchange sits against India's public-health commitments under the **WHO FCTC**. Article 17 of the FCTC asks parties to promote economically viable alternatives to tobacco growing.

### Scheme-in-focus: **Interest-Free Working Capital Assistance Scheme (FCV tobacco, Andhra Pradesh)**
- **Ministry:** Commerce & Industry (Department of Commerce). Tobacco is a commercial crop regulated by the **Tobacco Board** (a statutory body under the Tobacco Board Act, 1975, headquartered in **Guntur**).
- **Objective:** Give immediate liquidity to growers hit by slow sales in a weak market.
- **Key features:** (i) **₹50,000 per curing barn**, **interest-free**; (ii) paid by **DBT** into farmers' accounts; (iii) meant for repaying institutional loans, household needs and next-season inputs; (iv) aims to cut dependence on private moneylenders.
- **Beneficiaries/coverage:** About **44,000 farmers**, with a total outlay of about **₹220 crore**.
- **Significance:** A targeted, time-bound liquidity measure rather than a price support. Useful as an example of how trade shocks pass through to farm incomes.

**Destination notebook:** GS3 — Agriculture (commercial crops, farm credit); cross-tag GS2 Health (FCTC).

articles.title: A *dua* is not a religious appeal: Supreme Court leaves the Malegaon Central election standing — Polity & Governance
articles.text:
**Headline:** On **25 September 2026** a Bench of **Justices Vikram Nath, Sandeep Mehta and Augustine George Masih** dismissed the appeal of SP candidate Shaan E Hind Nihal Ahmed and upheld the **Bombay High Court's 8 June 2026** rejection of his election petition against AIMIM's **Mufti Mohammad Ismail Abdul Khalique** (Malegaon Central, Maharashtra, Nov 2024 election).

**Exam angle:** The cleanest live case on **Section 123(3), Representation of the People Act, 1951** — appeal to vote on grounds of religion as a "corrupt practice". The courts separated a religious *ritual* at a campaign gathering (the audience saying "Ameen") from an actual *appeal to vote* on religious grounds, and found the petition lacked the "material facts" a corrupt-practice charge needs. Read it against *Abhiram Singh* (2017), which read the section very broadly.

**Facts to memorise:**
- Margin in the original result: **162 votes** (1,09,653 vs 1,09,491); the petitioner himself polled 9,624.
- HC held: performing *dua* ≠ soliciting votes on religion; surrogates' speeches, support from religious organisations and general religious references in pamphlets did not make out **s.123(3) or s.123(4)**; petition dismissed **without trial** for want of material facts.
- Procedure: election petitions are tried by the **High Court** (s.80A), filed within **45 days** of the result (s.81); appeal lies to the **Supreme Court** (s.116A). A proven corrupt practice voids the election (s.100(1)(b)) and can lead to disqualification (s.8A).
- *Abhiram Singh v. C.D. Commachen* (2017), 7-judge Bench, **4:3** — "his religion" in s.123(3) covers the religion of the candidate, the agent **and the voter**.

**Destination notebook:** GS2 — Polity (Elections / Representation of the People Act).

**Static anchor:** *Laxmikanth*, "Elections" and "Electoral Reforms" chapters (RPA 1951 — corrupt practices and election disputes). **Nudge:** add a two-column box, "What *Abhiram Singh* bars / what *Malegaon* (2026) permits", and cross-link to Art. 329(b) (election disputes only by election petition).

articles.title: Ministry of Commerce & Industry (DPIIT): Make in India completes 12 years — PIB stocktake of manufacturing, FDI and PLI outcomes
articles.text:
Make in India was launched on **25 September 2014** to turn India into a global hub for manufacturing, design and innovation. On its 12th anniversary, the government put out a consolidated scorecard, and the Prime Minister summed it up as "more made in India, more investment, more exports".

**Why it matters:** This is the government's own balance sheet for its flagship industrial policy. Mains questions on deindustrialisation, PLI effectiveness and "Make in India vs. import dependence" need these baseline numbers. The release also shows the policy's new shape: sector-specific incentives such as PLI, semiconductors and rare-earth magnets now sit on top of the original ease-of-doing-business agenda.

**Key facts**
- Now called **Make in India 2.0**, it covers **27 sectors (15 manufacturing + 12 services)**.
- **Cumulative FDI of about US$ 843 billion** from 2014-15 to 2025-26.
- **Electronics production** rose from **₹1.9 lakh crore (2014-15) to ₹13.11 lakh crore (2025-26)**. India is the **world's 2nd-largest mobile phone manufacturer**.
- **Defence production** rose from **₹46,429 crore (2014-15) to ₹1.78 lakh crore (2025-26)**. **Crude steel** rose from **81.7 MT to 170 MT**, and India has been the 2nd-largest producer since 2018.
- **PLI schemes** cover **14 sectors**. Reported production and sales exceed **₹22 lakh crore** and jobs exceed **14 lakh** (sources give slightly different cut-off figures).
- Enablers: the **National Single Window System** (327 Central + 3,452 State approvals), the **India Industrial Land Bank** (4,220 parks mapped), **PM GatiShakti** and **Startup India** (about 2.54 lakh DPIIT-recognised start-ups).

### Initiative-in-focus: **Make in India**
- **Ministry:** Commerce & Industry, through **DPIIT**. **Launched:** 25 September 2014.
- **Objective:** Promote investment, foster innovation, build skills and create world-class manufacturing infrastructure.
- **Key features:** (i) four pillars: new processes, new infrastructure, new sectors and a new mindset; (ii) liberalised FDI, with the automatic route in most sectors; (iii) regulatory simplification through NSWS and ease-of-doing-business reforms; (iv) since 2020, sector-specific **PLI schemes** plus semiconductor and electronics-component missions.
- **Coverage:** 27 sectors under Make in India 2.0.
- **Significance:** Measures both the *scale* of output gains (electronics, defence, steel) and the *open questions* around domestic value addition and manufacturing's share of GDP. Use it to write a balanced Mains answer.

**Destination notebook:** GS3 — Economy (industrial policy, manufacturing, FDI).

articles.title: Ministry of Heavy Industries: European Parliament's ITRE Committee delegation holds industrial-cooperation talks in New Delhi
articles.text:
**What it is.** On **22 September 2026**, Union Minister for Heavy Industries and Steel **H. D. Kumaraswamy** held talks with an **eight-member delegation of the European Parliament's Committee on Industry, Research and Energy (ITRE)**, including MEPs **Raffaele Stancanelli** and **Angelika Winzig**. The discussion covered **industrial development, clean energy, electric mobility and industrial decarbonisation**.

**Why it matters.** This is the industrial-policy follow-through on the India–EU relationship after the conclusion of **FTA negotiations at the India–EU Summit earlier in 2026**. The substantive ask on India's side is **European participation in battery manufacturing** — a sector where India's **Advanced Chemistry Cell (ACC)** ambitions still depend on imported cell technology. Note also the decarbonisation angle: EU instruments such as **CBAM** make "greening" Indian steel a trade-access question, not only a climate one.

**Key facts.**
- **ITRE** is the European Parliament's standing committee on **industry, research and energy**.
- Indian schemes highlighted: **PLI for Automobiles and Auto Components**, **PLI for Advanced Chemistry Cell (ACC) Battery Storage**, and **PM E-DRIVE** for the EV ecosystem.
- **Global bidding for 10 GWh of ACC manufacturing capacity** is open, with a bid deadline of **13 October 2026**; European industry was invited to participate.
- Steel-sector cooperation discussed through **recycling and circular-economy** routes ("greening" of steel).
- Context: the **India–EU Summit of January 2026** concluded FTA negotiations and adopted a broader strategic-partnership agenda.

**Destination notebook:** GS3 — Economy (industrial policy, EV/battery manufacturing); cross-tag GS2 International Relations (India–EU).

---

### Also worth a line (22–23 September 2026)

- **Ministry of Coal** issued three backgrounders on 22 September — **CCL's transformation since 2014**, **CSR in Coal India Limited**, and **MCL's 10 lakh sq ft clean-up target** under Special Campaign 6.0.
- **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change / National Zoological Park** marked World Rhino Day with its **first Eco-Club Teachers' Orientation**, aimed at school outreach on wildlife conservation.
- **DPIIT / Ministry of Commerce and Industry** — Minister **Piyush Goyal** interacted with industry stakeholders on **ease of doing business, FTA utilisation and regulatory compliance** for exporters and MSMEs, with the **National Single Window System** in focus.
- **Vice-President C. P. Radhakrishnan** inaugurated the **9th India International Water Week 2026** at Bharat Mandapam on 22 September (flagged as upcoming in the 20 September briefing).
- **Ministry of Finance** — the Finance Minister, speaking on multilateral tax negotiations, noted that decisions taken over the next few years will **shape cross-border taxation for a generation**.

articles.title: Ministry of Commerce & Industry: India–New Zealand FTA to enter into force on 20 October 2026
articles.text:
**What it is.** The India–New Zealand Free Trade Agreement, signed on **27 April 2026** at Bharat Mandapam by Commerce & Industry Minister Piyush Goyal and New Zealand's Trade Minister Todd McClay, will **enter into force on 20 October 2026 (Vijaya Dashami)**. Both sides completed internal processes; the New Zealand Parliament passed the enabling legislation on **16 September 2026**. The date was announced jointly by the two ministers on 21 September.

**Why it matters.** This is India's newest FTA with a developed economy, and the template is the one UPSC keeps returning to: full market access on the export side, hard carve-outs on agriculture and dairy, and services/mobility as the real prize. It also operationalises the **India–New Zealand Strategic Partnership: Roadmap to 2030**, announced during PM Modi's **July 2026 visit to New Zealand — the first by an Indian PM in four decades**.

**Key facts and figures**
- **Goods (India's gains):** every tariff line covering **100% of India's exports** to New Zealand becomes duty-free from day one; New Zealand's peak tariffs of **up to 10%** are eliminated. Immediate gainers — textiles and apparel, leather and footwear, gems and jewellery, engineering goods, processed foods. India also gets duty-free inputs: wooden logs, coking coal, metal scrap.
- **Agricultural protection (India's carve-outs):** **dairy, animal meat (except sheep), key agricultural commodities, sugar and edible oils excluded** from tariff concessions.
- **Calibrated access for NZ:** apples, kiwifruit and **Manuka honey** get access only through **Tariff Rate Quotas (TRQs) with a Minimum Import Price and seasonal import windows**, plus safeguards.
